newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng seen testing 12,000 pts.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng seen testing 12,000 pts.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks look set for further gains this week with the Hang Seng index possibly testing 12,000 points after closing at its highest level since February 1994 on Friday, analysts said.
"The Hang Seng could challenge 12,000," said Alex Tang. head of research at Yamaichi International.
"Volume has increased considerably and with the increase in volume the market should be able to go higher from current levels."
The blue chip index hit a 1996 high on Friday at 11,788.41 before the closing the session at a 31-month high of 11,759.39, up 123.26 points. Over the week, the index rose 167 points, or 1.4 percent.

"The momentum may indeed carry over into the coming week. There is an absence of negative factors which should propel increased liquidity with also overseas participation," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"I think breaking 12,000 is possible," he said.

Analysts said they were optimistic about the earnings outlook for Hong Kong firms and were encouraged by signs of improving local fundamentals such as a recovering retail sector and strong property sales.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd is due to report its final results on Wednesday.

The U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged at last Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting had also removed some interest rate uncertainty out of the market, analysts said.

"The long bond yield has backed down to a more reasonable level," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. On Friday, the U.S. 30-year treasury bond slipped 8/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
"Probably the resistance level will be at around 12,000. I can't see any reason why it can't break through 12,000 very easily," said Boby Ho, dealing manager at GK Goh Securities.
"The index is now at a year high and I think the volume is pretty good so I can't see any big drop in the short-term."
Tang saw support for the Hang Seng at 11,500 points and predicted interest in market laggards would help the Hang Seng index move higher.
"Funds have been buying stocks which have been lagging behind and we have seen rotational buying."
However, Rossiter said Hong Kong stocks could consolidate around current levels if U.S. stocks fail to provide direction.
"I don't think the market is going to move up so much," Rossiter said.
The Dow struggled to a slightly higher finish on Friday as the market digested a flood of initial public offerings and investors prepared for spate of economic indicators.
This week Wall Street is facing the September National Association of Purchasing Management Index, August new home sales, leading indicators and Friday's key September employment data.
